title: Mushroomhead - Wikipedia
notes: Formed 1993 in Cleveland's Warehouse District as a side project; costumes, masks and pseudonyms to set it apart from the members' other bands; second show with GWAR at the Cleveland Agora; genres in the infobox alternative metal, industrial metal, nu metal, experimental metal; influences named for the band Mr. Bungle, Faith No More, Pink Floyd, Pantera, Nine Inch Nails, KMFDM; the 'X Face' logo on most members' masks; Dave Greathouse the band's video director, maskmaker and make-up artist; XX (Eclipse 2001, Universal reissue) sold nearly 40,000 in two to three months; Ozzfest 2002; the 'Solitaire/Unraveling' video; XIII (Universal, 2003) No. 40 on the Billboard 200; Skinny the only constant member: drums 1993-2022, studio drums since; percussion from 2006; samples, keyboards and production from 1993; in 2022 back injuries moved him off the live kit to DJ and water drums, with Aydin Kerr (credited as Aydin Michael in places) on live drums; Daniel 'Lil Dan' Fox touring water drummer from 2006; Dave 'Gravy' Felton, guitars, his brother; the Slipknot rivalry.

title: List of Mushroomhead band members - Wikipedia
notes: Skinny (Steve Felton) 1993-present: drums, percussion, keyboards, samples, water drums; production and visual direction; on every release. Lineup 2001-2004: Nothing, J Mann, Gravy, Pig Benis, Skinny (drums, percussion), Shmotz, Bronson, St1tch. Water drums: Skinny from late 2006; Daniel 'Lil' Dan' Fox 2006-2012 (left for Marilyn Manson and Dope); Rick 'St1tch' Thomas 2007-2022; Robert 'Roberto Diablo' Godsey 2012-2025; Aydin 'Alien' Kerr drums 2022 on (touring 2019 and 2022-2024).

title: XX (Mushroomhead album) - Wikipedia
notes: Eclipse Records, 8 May 2001; Universal reissue December 2001. Produced by Mushroomhead and Steve Felton; recorded 1994-1999; Universal version mixed by Toby Wright. Songs from Mushroomhead (1995), Superbuick (1996) and M3 (1999): Before I Die, Bwomp, Solitaire Unraveling, These Filthy Hands, Never Let It Go, Xeroxed, The Wrist, Chancre Sore, The New Cult King, Born of Desire, 43, Episode 29, and Pink Floyd's Empty Spaces (Universal). Skinny: drums. Billboard 200 No. 178, Heatseekers No. 6; over 300,000 sold (2011 source).

title: XIII (Mushroomhead album) - Wikipedia
notes: Universal, 14 October 2003; recorded 2002-2003 at Mars Studio, Shalersville, Ohio; produced by Mushroomhead, Steve Felton, Johnny K and Matt Wallace (mix). Skinny: drums, percussion; St1tch electronics, programming, samples, turntables; Shmotz keyboards, samples. Kill Tomorrow, Sun Doesn't Rise, Mother Machine Gun, Nowhere to Go, Becoming Cold (216), One More Day, The Dream Is Over (with Jens Kidman of Meshuggah), The War Inside, Almost Gone, Eternal, Our Own Way, Destroy the World Around Me, Thirteen (hidden Crazy, Seal's). Singles Sun Doesn't Rise (12 August 2003), Eternal, Kill Tomorrow. Billboard 200 No. 40; about 400,000 worldwide by 2006.

title: Zildjian, 'Sound Legacy - Skinny' (video, Rockstar Mayhem Festival, Mansfield, MA), 12 November 2014
notes: Read through YouTube's automatic captions, so quotes are as heard. Skinny: 'going back ... 86 87 really wanted to become a metal drummer; I was into bands like Megadeth, Metallica, Slayer, Sacred Reich'; 'got my first drum set when I was 16, I was a late starter, never took a lesson, taught myself everything'; he cracked cymbals ('it takes some finesse and some technique to hit a cymbal really hard and bash without breaking'); Zildjian 'the traditional sound'. Diablo describes the shared set-up: a 14-inch hat on the right and a closed 12-inch on the left, an 18-inch china at each side, the bell in the centre, a 12-inch china-splash on the left and a 10-inch splash on the right, two 18s and two 17s outside. Description lists, left to right: 18 A China High, 14 A Mastersound hats, 18 and 17 A Heavy Crash, 12 Oriental China 'Trash', 9 Zil-Bel, 10 A Splash, 17 and 18 A Heavy Crash, 21 A Mega Bell Ride, 12 A Custom Mastersound hats, 18 A China High. Songs: Our Apologies, The Dream Is Over.

title: JMann & Skinny, Mushroomhead 2002 interview (European press, spring 2002; uploaded by EraseTheDoubt, 2016)
notes: Audio only; read through automatic captions, so wording is approximate. Before their first Ozzfest ('this year we're playing the Ozzfest, the first time'). 'My name's Skinny, I'm the drummer.' First show at a Cleveland club, three days later 2,000 people at the Agora with GWAR; began as a side project. Up to Universal, everything on two-inch tape; Toby Wright's XX remix the first Pro Tools. J Mann: Skinny decides the mixing and mastering, the visual concepts, and 'by being the drummer ... the foundation musically'. Skinny: 'I'm really a drummer'; 'I'll bring like the hardcore gabber type techno ideas ... abrasive, 180 beats a minute'; Nightmare in Rotterdam, early Thunderdome, Rotterdam Records; 'we end our shows with a mix set of brutal hardcore'; three members worked on Integrity's Integrity 2000 (Victory).

title: RocknRollWorld Magazine, '20 minutes with Skinny from Mushroomhead' (video), uploaded 10 September 2015 (recorded on the 2014 tour)
notes: Automatic captions. The water drum: built by Skinny with Cleveland designer Dave Brooks; at first smaller, 'two drums', for an intermission piece of his own, percussion over programmed parts, 'a drum solo but not on a drum set'; plain water and white light worked best. 'Every album we change our masks'; masks sold through the band's mask and memorabilia page.

title: Chris Epting, 'Mushroomhead's Skinny on Family, Legacy + More', Loudwire, 30 July 2014
notes: Has played drums since the band began. A side project: 'Everybody was in other bands', playing doom, extreme and black metal; 'I didn't want to sound like Pantera or Nine Inch Nails'. Kiss (Cobo Hall, Detroit, late 1970s), the Residents and Bowie. The mask: 'The mask just unlocks so much. It allows the real self to emerge onstage'; 'a little bit murder and a little bit Darth Vader'.

title: Katarina McGinn, 'Mushroomhead - Still Learning, Still Hungry', Dead Rhetoric, 8 August 2024
notes: On drums: 'Its always been the heart and soul of the live machine'; 'The kick drum is almost as loud as the voice or guitars'; 'whereas before it was more of the backbone'; 'I'm a big fan of industrial metal. Anything percussive or theatrical'; 'The drums are very dear to me.' Kiss and Alice Cooper for the visuals; the Residents: 'There's no rules, you can do anything'; heavy, electronic and hip-hop together. Has produced the band's records for 30 years; each album 'its own little mini-movie'.

title: 'Water's Rage: An Interview with Mushroomhead's Steve "Skinny" Felton', The Nu Metal Agenda, 19 September 2024
notes: The water drums: 'a lot of that was truly inspired by Blue Man'; 'a huge addition to the live show'; lit from below, they change colour with the scenes. Pink Floyd's The Wall: 'To see an album go so cohesively with a visual has always kind of blown me away.' Sculpting, painting, mask making, audio engineering.

title: Greg Latham, 'Madness behind the Mask: An interview with Mushroomhead', Rock Sins, 30 July 2019
notes: 'Every album cycle each guy has his own mask and it changes a little, so you get a fresh sculpt done'; a uniform look between albums. The water drum began as 'literally just one drum and it was just for one act in a set'; 'ripping off Blue Man a little bit'. 'I got out from behind the drumset and it was an electronic piece.' 'Metal, hiphop, industrial to EDM.'

title: Paul Travers, 'How Mushroomhead survived nu metal and Slipknot feuds', Metal Hammer (Louder), 19 September 2024
notes: 'Back then I had big hopes and dreams that we'd be Metallica one day.' Drummer, leader and sole remaining original member. 1993: eight members of Cleveland bands, 'home-made horror masks' and pseudonyms; the 'masks-and-boiler suit image'. Kiss, Alice Cooper and the Residents ('they were doing whatever the fuck they wanted'); Mr. Bungle ('an example of how not giving a fuck could be done properly'). Swept up in nu metal: 'We got lumped into that category because that's how you pushed current bands.' Of Slipknot today: 'amazing'.

title: 'Would MUSHROOMHEAD Ever Perform Without The Masks? STEVE 'SKINNY' FELTON Responds', Blabbermouth, 17 July 2024
notes: 'your peripheral vision in a dark club, man - you can't see anything'; 'We have a lot of hand signals because there's no lip reading'; 'you do take on a little bit of a different character'.

title: Mushroomhead, 'Solitaire Unraveling' (official video, 2002; mushroomheadtv upload 2011)
notes: Looked at frame by frame (sepia-graded). Skinny at a kit in a cardboard desert: a close-fitting black hood over the whole head with the band's X face in white, thick dreadlocks from its crown hanging down his back and flicking up as he plays (1:15-1:19; 1:31-1:34 from overhead); a dark work jacket with an X-face patch on the sleeve; SABIAN on the cymbals (1:15).

title: Mushroomhead live, Ozzfest, Alpine Valley, East Troy, Wisconsin, 11 August 2002 (Liberated Tape Archive, complete show)
notes: Daylight. The band's uniform: black tactical vests and black shirts, urban-camouflage (white, grey, black) trousers and sleeves, white or red masks on the others. The kit (0:02-0:30, 11:34-11:40): black lacquer shells, a chrome rack across the front, four rack toms and floor toms, a dozen cymbals; the bass drum's front head white with the X face in black (X eyes, dripping teeth) inside a red ring. The drummer himself is hidden behind the cymbals throughout.

title: Mushroomhead live, Summerfest, Milwaukee, 27 June 2002 (Liberated Tape Archive, three cameras)
notes: Daylight. Red hoods with the X face in white on some members, J Mann in white face paint, black coats and vests, camouflage trousers; the bass drum's X-face head; the drummer behind the cymbals.

title: Mushroomhead live, Pierre's, Fort Wayne, Indiana, 21 November 2002, 'Skinny drum angle onstage' (Brad Nolan Videography)
notes: Camera on the riser behind and above him (red light). Thick dreadlocks hang from the back of his head over his shoulders to his shoulder blades. The kit from behind: four rack toms in a row across the bass drum with white coated heads, floor toms to his right, a ring of a dozen cymbals at one height on a rack, a closed hat on a remote at his left.
